question: The Deccan Plateau is a _________landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
solution:
The correct answer is __**triangular**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a **triangular** landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
 
• It is one of the largest plateaus in India, covering an area of about 1.9 million square kilometers.
 
• The plateau is bounded by the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats, which converge at the southern tip of India.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is known for its rich mineral resources and diverse ecosystems.
 
• The region is characterized by its elevated terrain, with an average elevation ranging from 100 meters to 1,000 meters above sea level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Deccan Plateau extends over eight Indian states, including Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and parts of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is rich in volcanic soils, which are beneficial for agriculture, particularly for growing cotton and other crops.
 
• The region has a significant historical and cultural heritage, with many ancient temples, forts, and monuments.
 
• The plateau is also home to several major rivers, including the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, which are vital for irrigation and water supply in the region.
 
• The climate of the Deccan Plateau varies from arid and semi-arid in the northwest to more humid conditions in the southeast.
